Theme 007 · Product UI as the stage

Inbox Choreography

A desktop mail client fills the frame. First it floods — alert emails, support tickets, digests of 38 dashboards, an unread counter that keeps climbing. With Acme Pulse on, rows auto-label, collapse and archive in rhythm until one calm email remains, and after the human answers it the inbox reaches zero.

COMPONENT KIT

  • Mail row — sender, subject, time; the unit of overload.
  • Unread badge — coral odometer that climbs to 147 and falls to 0 (green).
  • Auto-label chips — “summarised”, “normal”, “watched”, “anomaly”: Pulse triaging.
  • Swipe-reveal action — teal “Archived” bleeding in behind a row.
  • Digest email from Pulse — the single calm email with the anomaly card and two buttons.
  • Empty-state illustration — the pulse mark as an inbox-zero reward.

MOTION · MUSIC

  • Row collapse — height→0 with the rows below sliding up, 0.22 s power2.in, staggered on 1/16 notes (0.125 s at 120 BPM) for a rolling hi-hat feel.
  • Swipe triage — x 0→−100 % with the teal action colour bleeding in from the left, 0.25 s power3.in, one swipe per beat.
  • Counter countdown — 147→0 decelerating with expo.out over 2 bars, the last digit landing on a downbeat.

WHY / RISK · ADAPT IT

Why: everyone knows the dread of a flooded inbox and the relief of inbox zero, so the before/after is instant; one calm email from the agent is a believable, human-scale way to show “it filters the noise and asks you only once”. Risk: close to notification tropes — keep it desktop, typographic and slow in the proof beat.

Adapt to your product: the flood becomes whatever noise your customers drown in (tickets, alerts, requests); your product's single summary email carries the one decision it needs from them.
